title: How small is a haze particle?

segments.text: How small is a haze particle?
Haze is smoke from forest fires far away. Its smallest particles are less than two point five micrometres wide. That's about thirty times thinner than a strand of your hair!
Your nose hairs and mucus trap bigger dust. But these tiny particles can slip past, deep into your lungs. That's why haze makes it harder to breathe.
So why does an N ninety-five mask work better than a cloth one? Watch the full episode on Science Around Us.
